title: Open Small Business Records Taxonomy
classification_principle: Assign each record one primary family based on the part of the business accountable for the truth the record represents. Preserve other relevant contexts as relationships or metadata instead of competing primary copies.
accountability_test: If this record became wrong or disappeared tomorrow, who would have to deal with the consequence first?
tie_breakers: Classify by operational responsibility, not file format or generic document type.
Transaction evidence, accounting books, tax support, and remittance records default to Finance, accounting & tax when that is their primary purpose.
Customer commercial relationship records belong to Customers & revenue; execution records for a specific job or engagement belong to Projects, jobs & delivery.
Supplier-selection and procurement records belong to Vendors & procurement; resulting purchase invoices remain Finance when used as transaction evidence.
Employment and contractor relationship records belong to People & workforce; payroll journals and remittance evidence remain Finance when primarily financial.
Physical asset identity, service, inspection, warranty, and custody records belong to Assets & facilities; inventory movement and stock control belong to Inventory & supplies.

Licences and formal compliance evidence belong to Compliance, licences & safety; incident or claim handling belongs to Insurance, risk & incidents unless a specific compliance duty is the primary purpose.
Software ownership, access, configuration, recovery, and technology-service records belong to Technology, access & data.
Recurring methods belong to Operations & procedures; future-direction decisions belong to Strategy & planning; durable lessons and handoff context belong to Knowledge & continuity.
Required legal or regulatory systems of record are not displaced by this taxonomy. Use the taxonomy as a classification layer and preserve authority where the applicable rule requires it.

sensitivity_levels.context_dependent: Sensitivity varies materially with the particular record, business, customer, industry, and context.
sensitivity_levels.often_sensitive: This family often contains confidential, personal, commercial, location, account, or operational information that should be handled deliberately.
sensitivity_levels.highly_sensitive: This family commonly contains identity, financial, workforce, security, incident, access, legal-authority, or similarly consequential information.

recommended_record_metadata.purpose: Stable OSBRT family that owns the record's primary operational meaning.
Human record type without using it as the primary category.
Team, role, or business function accountable for correctness and follow-up.
Current business state such as active, draft, completed, superseded, closed, or archived.
Local handling cue appropriate to the specific record. The taxonomy family cue is not a legal classification.
When or why the record should be reviewed, renewed, superseded, or closed.
Other OSBRT families that materially relate to the same record without becoming competing primary homes.
Relevant customer, vendor, worker, project, asset, account, location, or other business entity references.
Pointer to the authoritative system, original, or governing record when the classified item is a representation or working copy. Never store secrets in this field.

categories.name: Governance & ownership
categories.definition: Records that establish the business entity, ownership, formal authority, governance structure, or major company decisions.
categories.accountability_cue: The owners, directors, officers, or people responsible for the company's legal identity and formal authority would need this to be correct.

applicability.when: Use for entity formation, ownership, formal authority, governance actions, and durable company-level decisions that are not better owned by a specific operating function.

sensitivity.note: These records can expose ownership, signatures, authority, identity, corporate structure, financing authority, or other consequential company information.

review_triggers: new, amended, or revoked governance document
major company decision requiring formal record

categories.name: Finance, accounting & tax
categories.definition: Accounting books, transaction evidence, banking, receivables and payables, expenses, reconciliations, financial reporting, tax, and financial-remittance records.
categories.accountability_cue: The person responsible for the books, cash, reporting, tax, or transaction evidence would need this to be correct.

applicability.when: Use when the record's primary purpose is to evidence, record, reconcile, report, pay, collect, remit, or support a financial or tax transaction or obligation.

sensitivity.note: Financial and tax records can expose account details, prices, margins, payroll information, tax identifiers, transactions, balances, and other high-impact business data.

review_triggers: retention requirement reached under the applicable authority

categories.name: Customers & revenue
categories.definition: Records that define, develop, manage, or document customer relationships, commercial opportunities, sales commitments, and ongoing customer accounts.
categories.accountability_cue: The person responsible for the customer relationship, sale, commercial commitment, or account would need this to be correct.

applicability.when: Use for customer and sales records whose main purpose is the commercial relationship rather than financial transaction evidence or execution of a specific job.

sensitivity.note: Customer records may contain personal information, pricing, commercial terms, correspondence, service history, or confidential customer information.

review_triggers: agreement signed, amended, renewed, or ended

categories.name: Vendors & procurement
categories.definition: Records used to source, evaluate, select, order from, manage, and communicate with suppliers and service providers.
categories.accountability_cue: The person responsible for the supplier relationship, purchase decision, order, or procurement process would need this to be correct.

applicability.when: Use for supplier and procurement records whose main purpose is selecting, ordering from, or managing a vendor rather than recording the resulting financial transaction or managing a technology system.

sensitivity.note: Vendor records may contain pricing, negotiated terms, contact information, account references, banking or payment details, and commercially sensitive correspondence.

categories.name: People & workforce
categories.definition: Employment, contractor, role, compensation-administration, time, training, performance, and other workforce records about people working for or with the business.
categories.accountability_cue: The person responsible for the worker relationship, role, employment administration, or workforce obligation would need this to be correct.

applicability.when: Use for records whose primary purpose is the working relationship or workforce administration. Payroll journals and remittance evidence remain Finance, accounting & tax when their main purpose is financial reporting or remittance.

sensitivity.note: Workforce records commonly contain identity, compensation, tax, banking, performance, health, schedule, disciplinary, or other sensitive personal information.

categories.name: Projects, jobs & delivery
categories.definition: Records that define, execute, change, approve, evidence, complete, or hand off specific customer work, projects, jobs, engagements, or deliverables.
categories.accountability_cue: The person accountable for delivering the specific piece of work would need this to be correct.

applicability.when: Use when the record's primary purpose is execution or delivery of a defined job, project, engagement, or deliverable rather than the general customer relationship or a recurring company procedure.

sensitivity.note: Delivery records may contain customer information, locations, specifications, pricing, approvals, photos, schedules, or confidential project material.

categories.name: Operations & procedures
categories.definition: Recurring operating procedures, checklists, schedules, instructions, quality methods, and routine process records used to run the business consistently.
categories.accountability_cue: The person responsible for how a recurring business process is performed would need this to be correct.

applicability.when: Use for repeatable operating methods and process controls. Classify meeting notes, plans, and checklists by their actual subject when they belong more naturally to a customer, project, workforce, safety, technology, or strategy context.

sensitivity.note: Some operating material is routine; other procedures can expose security, internal controls, customer handling, facility practices, or proprietary methods.

categories.name: Assets & facilities
categories.definition: Records that identify, assign, operate, service, inspect, repair, warrant, or manage physical assets, equipment, vehicles, tools, premises, and facilities.
categories.accountability_cue: The person responsible for the asset, equipment, vehicle, premises, or facility would need this to be correct.

applicability.when: Use when the record's main ongoing purpose is asset identity, custody, condition, operation, maintenance, warranty, inspection, or facility management. Purchase invoices remain Finance when their primary purpose is transaction evidence.

sensitivity.note: Asset and facility records can expose locations, serial numbers, access details ,
